newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican spot peso closes 5.5 centavos firmer.
newsitem.headline: Mexican spot peso closes 5.5 centavos firmer.

text.p: The peso closed sharply firmer Friday following a heavy inflow of dollars from foreign investors interested in taking positions in the Mexican financial markets, traders said.
"The peso firmed up quickly after dollars flooded into the market due to (lower) U.S. long bond rates," a trader said.

The peso closed 4.6 and 5.5 centavos stronger on 24-hour and benchmark 48-hour contracts to 7.5530/7.5580 and 7.5560/7.5600, respectively. Dollars were also in supply from some local brokers dumping long dollar positions due to liquidity arising from the entry of foreign investors.
"Dealers who went long on dollars yesterday out of concern over the (U.S. employment) figures, had to dump their positions and accept losses today," another peso trader said.

Investors were expecting the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield to rebound Friday following employment and unemployment data for August. But the figures ended up close to expectations and caused a U.S. markets rally.
The U.S. Department of Labor announced that 250,000 non-agricultural jobs were created in August, compared to market expectations of 244,000.
U.S. long bond yields were trading at 7.11 percent, compared to over 7.20 percent in early trade.
The same-day peso closed earlier 1.9 centavos firmer at 7.5600/7.5640 per dollar.

Peso traders estimated that the peso may hold steady at around 7.55 per dollar over the coming days, but could fall on expectations that domestic interest rates will fall at next week's primary auction.
